en.name: iNewsBoard
en.short_description: Headlines from BBC News, NPR and The Guardian, sorted by topic.
en.subtitle: Publisher feeds, by topic
en.description:
NewsBoard is a reader for news that other people report. It fetches 23 public news feeds from BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR and The Guardian, and shows you what those newsrooms published — their headline, their summary, their byline where they gave one, and the time they published it. NewsBoard writes none of it and changes none of it.

WHERE EVERY STORY COMES FROM
Every article carries the name of the publisher whose feed it arrived in, and opening one gives you a "Read at BBC News" button that takes you to that publisher's own page in your browser. Profile lists all four publishers with a link to each of their sites. If a feed does not supply something — a picture, a byline, a summary — that space is left empty rather than filled in.

BY TOPIC
Technology, business, science, health, politics, sport, entertainment, environment and world, plus a For You view built from the topics you pick and a Trending view. Trending here means one thing only: the same story is being carried by more than one of the publishers. There is no popularity score, no view count and no ranking, because nothing in the app measures any of those.

READ LATER, FOLLOW, SEARCH
Save any article to read later; saved articles stay on your device. Share a story through your phone's share sheet. Follow a topic or a hashtag and the Following tab collects the stories that mention it. Search runs across the headlines, summaries, publishers and tags of everything that has loaded.

OFFLINE, HONESTLY
The last set of stories NewsBoard successfully downloaded is kept on the device. With no connection it shows that set and says "Offline · showing stories saved 2h ago" above it, so you always know how old what you are reading is. With nothing downloaded yet it tells you the fetch failed and offers a retry, instead of showing you an empty page that looks like a quiet news day.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
No account, no sign-in. No advertising. No subscription and no in-app purchase — there is no paid tier and nothing is held back. Nothing in NewsBoard is generated: no AI summaries, no rewritten headlines. There is no push notification.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
NewsBoard is a reader for news that other people report. It fetches 23 public news feeds from BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR and The Guardian, and shows you what those newsrooms published — their headline, their summary, their byline where they gave one, and the time they published it. NewsBoard writes none of it and changes none of it.

Intended audience:
Publisher feeds, by topic

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. The first launch shows one screen where you pick topics for the For You view; after that the six tabs (Home, Trending, Search, Following, Saved, Profile) hold every feature. Profile > About links the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Support pages.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- The publishers' public RSS feeds over HTTPS: feeds.bbci.co.uk (BBC News, BBC Sport), feeds.npr.org (NPR) and www.theguardian.com (The Guardian). The app has no backend of its own and no account system.
- Google Firebase (Crashlytics crash reports, Analytics, Performance Monitoring) through the shared agl_observability package, active in release builds when the Firebase configuration is bundled.
- Article links and the policy pages open in the device browser.

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The interface is in English. Tab labels, a few shared strings and system controls follow the device language in 12 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish); there is no in-app language picker. Articles are in the language their publisher wrote them in, which is English for all 23 feeds. Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry. It shows third-party news content: the headline, summary, byline, image and publication time from the publishers' own public RSS feeds (BBC News, BBC Sport, NPR, The Guardian). Every item is attributed to its publisher by name and links to the publisher's own page; NewsBoard writes, rewrites and summarises none of it. Profile lists each publisher with a link to its site. The app's artwork and interface copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

Both numbers exclude the ~60 widgets every Flutter app uses — Column, Text,
Padding and so on. Including them makes any two Flutter apps look 97% alike,
which is a property of the framework rather than of these apps.

The store copy is distinct on the same basis: no two of the 43 share more
than 22% of their description vocabulary.

6. COULD THIS BE AN IN-APP PURCHASE IN ANOTHER APP
No. No other app on this account is in its category (NEWS), so there is no existing app it could be an in-app purchase or feature of.

7. CODE SHARED WITH OUR OTHER APPS
Yes, infrastructure only: agl_i18n (shared translations); agl_observability (crash reporting). It does not use Supabase and has no sign-in. No screens, features or content are shared; the similarity figure in 5 measures exactly that.

8. CODE SHARED WITH THIRD-PARTY APPS
No, beyond standard third-party frameworks: flutter_localizations, flutter_riverpod, share_plus.
